extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom managers, journalism students, and media researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Apply Tuchman's typifications and newsroom-routine factors to understand or decide which events become news and how they are covered (e.g., placement, speed, resources). Useful for analyzing newsroom decision-making and for reporters/editors planning coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard News
rubrics_metrics.description: Time-sensitive, government, major crime, disasters. Goes on front page; written quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hard news stories are prioritized for immediate coverage and front-page placement; they fit tight production schedules and demand rapid reporting and quick turnaround.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soft News
rubrics_metrics.description: Human interest, lifestyle. Less urgent; can wait.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Soft news can be scheduled or delayed for better placement or fuller treatment; it is less tied to immediate events and allows more time for feature-style writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spot News
rubrics_metrics.description: Unscheduled events that just happened. Requires fast reaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spot news triggers rapid newsroom mobilization; coverage depends on immediate reporter/photographer availability and the ability to transmit copy quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing News
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that unfold over time. Allows planned coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developing stories can be followed across multiple editions; they permit some forethought and allocation of resources to cover subsequent developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing News
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories scheduled in advance (legislation, trials). Easiest to plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuing news fits editorial calendars and beats, enabling systematic planning and predictable resource assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictability of unfolding
rubrics_metrics.description: Easier-to-routinize events get covered; how foreseeable an event's development affects news selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events whose trajectories are predictable fit newsroom typifications and routines better, making them more likely to be assigned and followed; unpredictable events may be ignored if they cannot be routinized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time horizon
rubrics_metrics.description: Fits production schedule — whether an event is immediate, ongoing, or schedulable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compatibility with deadlines and edition cycles determines whether and how an event is covered (e.g., spot vs. continuing vs. soft).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an event falls within a reporter's beat or the newsroom's geographic focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events concentrated in capital cities, courthouses, or other covered locations are more likely to be noticed and covered because they lie within the 'news net.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Source availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of official spokespeople and predictable sources who can be contacted for quotes and verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events with accessible, authoritative sources are easier to cover; lack of sources makes stories harder to routinize or verify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of staff, photographers, transmission means (e.g., satellite) to cover an event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even newsworthy events may go uncovered if the newsroom lacks personnel or technical means to report them in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial planning compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an event can be incorporated into existing editorial plans, schedules, and story agendas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that fit editors' plans are favored; those that conflict with planning cycles or priorities may be downplayed or omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Net — geographical concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsrooms concentrate attention geographically (capital cities, courthouses) to cast a 'news net.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This spatial focus structures which events enter journalists' awareness; remote or dispersed events are less likely to be captured by the net.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Net — topic-specific specialization (beats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialization by topic (beats) channels reporters' attention to certain institutions and subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beats create predictable source networks and event types that feed typifications; events outside beats have fewer pathways into coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Net — time-based routines
rubrics_metrics.description: Time-based routines (scheduled press conferences, regular briefings) shape what events are visible to journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routines produce a steady flow of news-access points that fit typifications and ease planning; unscheduled events must penetrate these routines to be noticed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational construction of news
rubrics_metrics.description: What gets defined as news is produced by organizational routines, available typifications, and the 'news net' of beats and sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsworthiness is not an intrinsic property of events; analysts and practitioners should evaluate selection decisions in light of organizational constraints, typification categories, and the structural means by which events reach journalists.
